items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: I did, on the strength of what Hag said... I told Hag, 'Well, we have no work for a month...'

ctx.x: He said he wished that I would. Well,

I did, on the strength of what Hag said, he sort of persuaded me, I stayed on. I did turn it down, but then when we came to Europe the next time, I told Hag, 'Well, we have no work for a month, and look at the scene and see -- I will just stay over, I didn't say I was definitely going to stay and we're in the Rotterdam Airport and most of the guys in the band -- we had finished the tour in Holland and the guys are going back now to London and then the States, and I am just going to London, where I have been now…

And a Dutch impressario came running up to me, all out of breath before we went in to get on the plane and he said, 'Mr. Freeman, would you want to stay over here and do some work in Holland? There's a big festival coming up called the Brada Festival, and he offered me a tremendous amount of money for -- just to play one hour, and so the agent, Robert Masters, who was handling us on the road, said, 'My God, how are you that they would offer that kind of money, because he had never been in the solo field, he had…
